# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection — Host 10.2.28.88

**Capture:** 2026-02-28-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap (15,512 packets, 2026-02-28 23:55:06 to 2026-03-01 04:16:35 UTC+4)

## Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 10.2.28.88 |
| MAC address | 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR |
| AD domain | EASYAS123 (easyas123.tech) |
| Logged-in user | brolf (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, frames to/from DC 10.2.28.2) |

Host obtained its address via DHCP (frame 2, requested 10.2.28.88, hostname DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR) and is domain-joined to a Windows Server DC at 10.2.28.2 (easyas123-dc.easyas123.tech).

## Malware Family

**NetSupport Manager RAT (NetSupport Client), commercial remote-access tool abused as a RAT.**

Attribution is **signature-confirmed**, not just behavioral, based on two independent artifacts in the traffic itself:

1. HTTP `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` on every C2 request (e.g., frame 2638 onward).
2. Decoded HTTP POST bodies contain the literal NetSupport client-server protocol keywords `CMD=POLL`, `INFO=1`, `ACK=1` and `CMD=ENCD`, `ES=1`, `DATA=<hex-encoded blob>` — this is the documented NetSupport beacon/poll protocol, sent to the well-known callback path `/fakeurl.htm`.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint:**
- `45.131.214.85:443` (TCP) — plaintext HTTP carried on port 443, no TLS handshake present (confirmed: 0 TLS records on this stream) — a known NetSupport RAT evasion trait.

**Malicious domain:**
- `vadusa.xyz` — queried twice by the victim (frames 1559, 1747) before the DC resolved it (frame 2566, `A vadusa.xyz -> 45.131.214.85`). Victim connected directly to the resolved IP for all subsequent C2 traffic.

**Malicious URL:**
- `http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm` — POST target for all C2 traffic, 264 requests over the full ~4.35-hour capture window (first at t+45.05s, last at t+15682.04s), consistent with periodic RAT check-in/beaconing (roughly every 60 seconds).

**Transferred files / hashes:**
- None observed. No executable, script, or binary object was transferred over HTTP in this capture (`--export-objects http` and URI search for `.exe/.msi/.ps1/.hta/.dll/.zip/.rar/.7z` returned no hits). All payload data exchanged with 45.131.214.85 is small, hex-encoded C2 telemetry embedded in `CMD=ENCD` POST bodies, not file transfers. No SHA256 can be grounded in this evidence; the initial infection vector (how the NetSupport client was delivered/installed) is not captured in this pcap.

## Summary

10.2.28.88 (DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR, user brolf) is actively beaconing to a NetSupport Manager RAT C2 server at vadusa.xyz / 45.131.214.85 over HTTP on TCP/443, sustained for the full capture duration. All other external traffic from the host (Microsoft/Windows Update/Office telemetry, Adobe, Akamai/Azure CDN ranges) is benign background noise. No secondary payload delivery or lateral movement was observed in this capture; recommend isolating the host and inspecting it for the NetSupport client installation artifacts on disk.
